headline: Profit rebounds on derivative gains, spot power strength
summary_short: AES swung to $426M net income attributable to the company in Q2 2026 (diluted EPS $0.60) from a $95M loss ($0.15/share loss) a year ago, as revenue rose 20% y/y to $3,422M on higher spot power sales and energy-derivative gains.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue rose 20% y/y to $3,422M, led by $295M higher Renewables revenue (energy-derivative gains, Colombia spot sales, U.S. development services) and $190M higher Energy Infrastructure revenue (Argentina spot sales). Operating margin expanded 53% to $692M. Net income attributable to AES swung to $426M ($0.60 diluted EPS) from a $95M loss ($0.15/share loss) a year ago, aided by a smaller other-expense charge, an 83% drop in income tax expense, and a $186M gain on the partial Fluence share sale; partly offset by a prior-year Mong Duong valuation-allowance benefit. Cash rose to $1,800M; equity grew to $4,942M. No forward guidance was given — AES stopped disclosing Adjusted EPS/EBITDA in Q1 2026, and a take-private merger is pending.

drivers.explanation: Q2 net income swung to $387M from a $150M loss on favorable energy-derivative marks, higher U.S. development-services contributions, stronger spot energy/capacity sales, higher AES Ohio retail margin, and a Fluence gain; partly offset by a prior-year Mong Duong valuation benefit and the Maritza PPA expiration.

$295M higher at Renewables (energy-derivative gains, higher Colombia spot sales/prices, U.S. development services, new projects), $190M higher at Energy Infrastructure (Argentina spot sales, Mexico spot sales, LNG sales), and $64M higher at Utilities (AES Ohio rate settlement, transmission/rider revenue).

Not explained in the release as a standalone line; the rise is consistent with higher spot energy/capacity purchase volumes implied by the $239M y/y operating-margin gain against the $567M revenue increase.

Operating margin rose $239M mainly on higher Renewables margins from energy-derivative gains and U.S. development-services contributions, plus higher Energy Infrastructure spot sales/prices; partly offset by lower contract sales volume from the expired Maritza PPA in Bulgaria.

Not explained in the release as a standalone line; the swing reflects the $239M operating-margin gain, a $268M smaller other-expense charge, and a $139M Fluence-driven gain on disposal, partly offset by a $184M swing in asset impairment expense.

Income tax expense fell $139M (83%) as the effective rate dropped from 428% to 6% on ITC benefits and the Fluence sell-down valuation-allowance release, adding to the swing from a $150M net loss to $387M net income.
Not explained in the release as a standalone line; the swing to $0.60 tracks the $521M improvement in net income attributable to AES against a roughly flat 715M weighted diluted share count.
Not explained in the release as a standalone balance-sheet line; consistent with operating cash flow up $726M year-to-date, partly used for a $3.47B year-to-date capex program and debt repayments.

Not explained in the release as a standalone line; consistent with $913M of six-month net income retained and a $115M favorable other-comprehensive-income swing, partly offset by dividends and noncontrolling-interest transfers.
Not explained in the release; the company made no repurchases under its buyback program in the quarter, leaving the diluted share count essentially unchanged y/y.
